---
title: "Parameter statistics"
---

Basic descriptive statistics for every analyte — the "per-parameter basic
statistics" section of the report outline.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import sfer_common as sfer

sfer.style()
df = sfer.load()
```

## Summary statistics

```{python}
#| echo: false
table = sfer.stats_table(df).round(3)
table["n"] = table["n"].map("{:,}".format)
table
```

## Distributions

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Distribution of temperature across all samples."
#|   - "Distribution of salinity across all samples."
#|   - "Distribution of CTD dissolved oxygen across all samples (the one impossible reading above 15 mg/L is excluded)."
#|   - "Distribution of Winkler dissolved oxygen across all samples."
#|   - "Distribution of ammonium across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of phosphate across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of nitrate + nitrite across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of nitrate across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of nitrite across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of silicate across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of chlorophyll a across all samples (log scale)."
#|   - "Distribution of pheophytin across all samples (log scale)."
log_cols = {"nh4", "po4", "no3_no2", "no3", "no2", "si", "chl", "pheo"}
for col in sfer.ANALYTES:
    s = df.loc[sfer.plausible(df, col), col]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4))
    if col in log_cols:
        s = s[s > 0]
        bins = np.logspace(np.log10(s.min()), np.log10(s.max()), 40)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
    else:
        bins = 40
    ax.hist(s, bins=bins, color="#1f78b4", alpha=0.85)
    ax.set_title(sfer.label(col))
    ax.set_ylabel("samples")
    ax.set_xlabel(sfer.units(col))
```

The physical properties (temperature, salinity) and both oxygen measures are
roughly symmetric, whereas the nutrients and the pigments are strongly
right-skewed — a few high values trace to blooms and coastal inputs — which is
why those plots use log axes. Note that **nitrate + nitrite** is simply the sum
of the **nitrate** and **nitrite** columns, so the three are not independent.

How each of these properties changes with depth — surface, mid and bottom
bottles — is the subject of the [Vertical structure](vertical.qmd) page, which
shows a depth-class violin for every analyte.

::: {.callout-note}
**A note on oxygen units.** The two oxygen columns are on different scales:
`o2_ctd` is in mg/L while `o2_disc` (Winkler titrations) is in µmol/kg. `o2_ctd`
also contains one physically impossible reading (~6,000 mg/L) that is excluded
from the plots but kept in the summary table above. `o2_disc` is only available
for a small number of samples, so its distribution is correspondingly rough.
:::
